positions.name: Deere & Company
positions.catalyst: FQ3 2026 reported before the open THIS MORNING (Aug 20) and beat a bar the sell side had been cutting into. Diluted EPS $5.10 vs ~$4.70-4.72 consensus (~8% beat) and up 7% y/y; net sales and revenues $12.608B, +6% y/y; equipment-operations net sales $10.999B, +6%. Net income $1.379B, +7%. Construction & Forestry was the engine — net sales $3.618B, +18% y/y, with segment operating profit roughly $237M to $436M (~+84%) and the FY26 C&F margin outlook set at 10.5-11.5%; Small Ag & Turf sales $3.383B, +12%, operating profit $485M to $622M. Management RAISED the FY2026 net-income floor to $4.75-5.0B from the $4.5-5.0B range carried since May (itself a raise off the $4.00-4.75B November 2025 outlook), and guided FY26 equipment-operations operating cash flow to $5.0-5.5B. This is the 16th straight EPS beat and the 28th straight revenue beat.
positions.driver: Best risk/reward on the board today because the gap is small and the invalidation sits under the entire move. DE is bid $598.00/$600.00 pre-market against a $580.63 close — only +3.3%, so there is nothing to chase, yet a 5% stop at $570.00 sits BELOW yesterday's $579.31 low and below a complete gap-fill at $580.63: the trade can give back the whole earnings pop and still not stop out. That is the asymmetry the book is supposed to buy. The setup is also a textbook lowered-bar beat — 18 downward EPS revisions versus 5 upward went into this print, consensus had EPS declining y/y, and Deere delivered growth instead. Overhead is open: DE is ~11% below its $674.19 February 52-week high, and $600 reclaims yesterday's $596.06 high. The tape favors it too — Wednesday's session was tech-weak with health care and cyclicals bid, and DE is a liquid ($157B cap, ~1.0M shares/day) industrial cyclical rather than another AI-semi name, which is precisely what cost this book money on KEYS yesterday. Runners-up were rejected on skew, not quality: NDSN posted a record quarter with backlog +35% and a raised FY guide but is already +6.5% pre-market at ~$331 versus a $315.68 52-week high, so any gap-fill to $309.92 is a stop-out; BILL's FY27 EPS guide of $3.56-3.79 is strong but the stock is only +1.7% and the market has repeatedly refused to pay for it; ADI beat ($3.45 vs $3.34) but is only +0.8% and carries the same AI-semi tape risk that just broke KEYS; AAP beat on EPS ($1.03 vs $0.81) yet is indicated down ~12%, a clear guidance problem; WMT had not printed at run time.
positions.risks: The core ag franchise is still in recession and the raise did not fix it — Deere's own FY26 industry outlook has U.S./Canada large ag down 15-20% and South America down 15-20%, July retail sales show large tractors down 7% and combines down 20% industry-wide, and Deere dealer inventories of 100+ PTO hp tractors sit at 33% of trailing retail versus 31% a year ago. Production & Precision Ag operating profit actually FELL ($580M to $527M) on volume and warranty, so the beat leaned on Construction & Forestry and Small Ag — a mix the bears will call low quality, and the FY2027 order-book gap is the open question analysts will press on the 9:00am CT call, which is the single biggest same-day risk: a soft FY27 order commentary can reverse the gap intraday. Valuation offers no cushion — 33x trailing earnings after a 26-32% YTD run, so 'good but priced in' is a live verdict. Macro is unhelpful: Jackson Hole begins today, Walmart's print this morning sets the consumer tone, and yesterday's FOMC minutes left rate-path uncertainty; a risk-off session can overwhelm a single beat. Finally, a 5% stop on a $600 stock is a real $389 of capital at risk against a book that has drawn down to $7,774.
